Answer: D
Reason: The chest X-ray shows complete opacification of the right hemithorax with a contralateral (leftward) mediastinal shift, which indicates a space-occupying lesion such as a massive pleural effusion or large tumor rather than atelectasis (which causes ipsilateral shift). The homogeneous density and patient age make a large pleural-based mass (e.g., mesothelioma) or massive effusion the most likely diagnosis among the choices implying mass effect.
